overview.body:
# See a Plan as a hierarchy of names

A pile of Tasks hides the shape of the work. This Plan gives a Plan a few top-level **names** that zoom into more detailed names, down to the parts expected to be worked on. Tasks name the names they work on, so a name is checked off as its Tasks finish, and work on no name, or a name no Task reaches, stands out. [The work is one new record, a field on Tasks, and what is derived from them](annotation:the-work).

## Where names live

A name is a record of the Plan, beside its Tasks: `names/<id>.name/name.json` holds a title, an optional summary, at most one parent, labeled links to other names, and an optional pointer to a Term, Component, or System. Git is its history. It carries no code; its code is the code of the Tasks under it.

## What is derived

Each name's progress rolls up from the Tasks that name it or any name beneath it: done when all are done, under way when any has started. `plan guide` lists Tasks on no name and names no Task reaches, but only for a Plan that has names, and never refuses anything.

## What a reader sees

A Names tab beside Deck and Tasks shows the hierarchy as a tree and as a diagram laid out from it: the focused name's children as boxes, each showing its own children in miniature. Selecting a box zooms in; a breadcrumb zooms out. Links are drawn between the visible boxes holding their ends.
